The physician may be found liable if the material risks of cervical treatment, including vertebrobasilar injury, were not explained and informed consent was not obtained before articulatory springing. Confusion, nausea, and vertigo hours later are a known rare vascular complication and do not by themselves prove negligence when consent was adequate and the technique met the standard of care. Cervical osteoarthritis is common at this age and is not an absolute bar to gentle articulatory treatment.

CONFIDENCE: 74
